findings.text: The tree exposes a predicate that classifies a 32 bit counter index as a compatibility backdoor counter. It affirms the host TSC view, the real time view and the apparent time view, and denies all other values, letting callers bypass normal privilege checks for those three selectors.

Debug register payloads are accepted only when the upper 32 bits are all zero. Both the control validation and the status validation enforce the same width rule, rejecting any value with a nonzero high half.

The virtualization enable gate obtains the register named by MSR_EFER through the emulator operation table and requires the bit named by EFER_SVME. A clear bit leads to an invalid opcode fault outcome, while a set bit leads to continuation.

The address qualified virtualization gate reads the accumulator register named by VCPU_REGS_RAX and asks the page address validator about that guest address. An invalid address leads to a general protection fault with zero error code, otherwise evaluation proceeds to the virtualization enable gate.

The timestamp read gate inspects control register four and the current privilege level. When the disable flag named by X86_CR4_TSD is set together with nonzero privilege, the outcome is a general protection fault with zero code, otherwise continuation.

The counter read gate loads control register four and the selector from the register named by VCPU_REGS_RCX. When the global backdoor enable is active and the selector is classified as a backdoor counter, access is granted at once. Otherwise a fault with zero code results when unprivileged access lacks the enable flag named by X86_CR4_PCE or when an early vendor hook rejects the selector; otherwise the gate continues.

Port permission checks for string and immediate port operations first limit the byte count to four and then query the IO permission helper with port and limited width. Denial produces a general protection fault with zero code, approval produces continuation. Input checks limit the destination width while output checks limit the source width.

Decode tables are built from a compact constructor vocabulary. Each entry encodes operand and mode flags, optionally an intercept identity, optionally a pre execution permission routine, and optionally an execution routine. Companion constructors express paired byte and wider forms, dual selection by mode or prefix or operand direction, group selection by extension field, and escape selection for coprocessor opcodes. A single shared entry denotes unimplemented slots that fault as invalid opcode.

Protected mode system secondary dispatch splits by extension field. The first subgroup implements only a privileged hypercall, the second only monitor and wait intercepts, the third only control register extension writes, the fourth eight host operations for run, call, load, save, interrupt gating, secure init and address invalidation with SVM gating, and the last only timestamp reads with privilege gating. All remaining slots in those subgroups are unimplemented. A mode dual chooses between legacy descriptor table handling and the extension dispatch.

Extension selected arithmetic and logic groups provide the expected integer operations with locking and page table hints where relevant. Coverage includes add variants, logical or and and, subtract variants, xor, compare without writeback, rotates and shifts, test, negate and complement, widening multiply and divide, increment and decrement in byte and wider forms, indirect calls and jumps with push, system segment descriptor loads and stores, immediate bit test with set clear and complement, plus a memory stack pop entry.

The single byte primary map densely covers arithmetic, data movement, string, stack, branch and flag operations, leaving selected slots unimplemented. Gated entries attach IO permission checks to port and string transfers, protection and privilege flags to system instructions, dedicated access checks to control and debug register moves, privilege checks to timestamp and counter reads, and intercept identities to descriptor, cache and halt operations. Coprocessor escapes remain largely unimplemented except for control word store, status word store and initialization. Dual entries handle address size dependent sign extending moves and effective address calculation without memory access.

The two byte map focuses on system control, vector moves and bit manipulation. Control and debug register moves use dedicated access gates, timestamp and counter reads use privilege gates, and descriptor, cache maintenance and serializing operations use intercepts. Prefix selected subgroups discriminate aligned versus unaligned vector moves and integer versus vector forms. Companion dual groups provide atomic wide compare exchange with a process identifier extension, simple moves, state save and restore, and cache line flush variants.

The three byte map with 38 escape is almost entirely unimplemented. Only the final two slots implement byte swapped moves in opposite register and memory directions with emulation on invalid opcode, and one mid range slot reuses the shared aligned vector move subgroup.

Shadow stack relevance follows a single flag on the decoded descriptor. Branch tracking relevance requires the branch flag, then treats far transfers as indirect except for far returns, system exit and interrupt return. Near branches are indirect when sourced from register or memory and direct when lacking a source or using an immediate source. Far direct encodings and unexpected source kinds trigger warning paths.

Immediate operand width follows the byte operation flag, else the ambient operand width, with eight byte ambient width reduced to four. Decoding reads one, two, four or eight bytes with sign extension, then either keeps the extended value or masks to the narrow width for unsigned uses.
The high 32 bits of debug control and debug status values are reserved and must be zero; bits above position 31 carry no payload.

A global compatibility enable creates a narrow privilege exception for three backdoor counter selectors, permitting user mode reads that would otherwise fault when the counter enable flag is clear. An implementation must confine the exception to exactly those selectors and must still apply the early rejection hook to all other selectors.

Pre execution gates share three exits: continue, fault as invalid opcode, or fault as general protection with zero code. Address validation precedes virtualization enable checks, privilege checks precede timestamp and counter execution, and port permission checks precede port and string execution. A fault exit suppresses the main execution routine for that instruction.

Six small routines act as table attached pre execution entries invoked by the decoder before the main execution routine: virtualization enable, address qualified virtualization enable, timestamp privilege, counter privilege, input port permission and output port permission.
